# Jumbo & GrowthBook | Introduction Call
Date: 2026-09-25 | Duration: 33.439998626708984m

## Summary
Jumbo is a family-owned Dutch supermarket with 20% market share in the Netherlands, owns Hema, and has approximately 105 developers working with AWS, Java, and GraphQL. Its A/B testing setup is fragmented: a side-spec DOM manipulation tool is used poorly, newsletter testing is isolated but acceptable, and Bloombreach search testing has poor quality. Jumbo has no feature toggles and currently uses on/off releases, but it has started a GrowthBook proof of concept for feature toggles and A/B testing on test and acceptance clusters, with production rollout planned within days. Because the free version lacks role-based access, Jumbo built a companion app through the API to give business users experiment visibility and basic toggle control without broad admin access. Jumbo is considering the paid version for role-based access, compliance, and SSO, with approximately 50k tentatively reserved for next year. Discussions also covered training, experiment culture, pricing models, phased onboarding, deferred payment options, a follow-up on setup and SSO, and opening a Slack channel that includes engineer Jeremy French.

## Keywords
AB testing, feature toggles, GrowthBook, experimentation culture, role-based access, Jumbo supermarket

# JUMBO & GrowthBook | POC, Governance, Commercials
Date: 2026-09-29 | Duration: 47.7400016784668m

## Summary
The discussion focused on adopting a self-hosted experimentation platform with Okta authentication, role-based access, and no feature limitations in the enterprise self-hosted version. Licensing options included annual per-user pricing, differentiated full and read-only access, tiered pricing, and an experiment-based model supporting unlimited users through per-experiment fees. Feature management would use a companion app controlled through an API, while experimentation could use frontend, backend, or edge SDKs. A Chrome-based visual editor supports UI, text, and CSS changes, with AI assistance and Figma imports, although a developer-first approach favors backend changes for larger experiments. Sticky bucketing maintains user variant consistency, which the Open Feature SDK lacks. A proof of concept is planned for Oct-Nov on jumbo.com, covering flag creation, experiment launch, results review, and Databricks integration. Internal teams are supportive, a Slack channel awaits approval, and the data team will investigate the Databricks setup. Budget discussions and a possible replacement of the existing SiteSpect contract remain ongoing.

## Keywords
Feature toggles, experimentation, self-hosted, licensing model, Databricks integration, POC governance
